issue.title: status: retry conflicts without blocking queued updates

labels.name: user-8213b3f8/repo-e5e4d80a
labels.description: Denotes a PR that changes 100-499 lines, ignoring generated files.

issue.body:
The status manager currently drops writes that hit a resourceVersion conflict. If the controller has already processed an update but the writer's cache is still behind, the write fails and may not be queued again when the cache catches up. Status can stay stale until another event or edit.

Retry conflicts with backoff, reading the cache again on each attempt. Requeueing releases the worker so a conflicting resource cannot block other updates. Newer queued work takes precedence, and UID/generation checks prevent old work from being applied after deletion/recreation or a generation change.

Adds regression tests for worker fairness, newer queued updates, deletion/recreation, and shutdown. The follow-up Route change includes a [delayed-cache reproduction](https://github.com/cam-garrison/istio/blob/fb0e9a4e9a798a650e7468c871bd9e27977e64a7/pilot/pkg/config/kube/gatewaycommon/route_status_test.go#L446) that fails without retries and converges without another Route event.

Validated with `go test -race` across the seven affected packages (472 tests/subtests) and ran a controlled reproduction against a fresh kind API server failed 3/3 on upstream and recovered 3/3 with the worker patch, without another enqueue. Writer-cache lag was deliberately injected.

Updates `github.com/quic-go/quic-go` from 0.64.1 to 0.65.0
Release notes

Sourced from github.com/quic-go/quic-go's releases.

v0.65.0

This release updates qlog to the latest IETF drafts, adds explicit stream credit release, and fixes a number of HTTP/3 and connection migration bugs.

  • With Config.RequireStreamCreditRelease, completed streams count towards the incoming stream limit until the application calls ReleaseStreamCredit: #5981, #5982
  • qlog: events now follow draft-ietf-quic-qlog-quic-events-14 and draft-ietf-quic-qlog-h3-events-14: #6120

Breaking Changes

  • http3: HTTPStreamer.HTTPStream now returns (*Stream, error), and no longer sends an implicit 200 response: #5988, #5994

Notable Fixes

  • QUIC v2 key updates now use the correct quicv2 ku label: #5973
  • Connections using zero-length connection IDs no longer stop receiving packets after version negotiation: #6129
  • Switching paths now uses a new connection ID, fixing servers that kept sending to the old address after repeated NAT rebindings: #6015
  • Clients now send PATH_RESPONSE on the path the PATH_CHALLENGE was received on: #5980
  • Path.Probe now succeeds on an already validated path: #6019
  • Reordered and retransmitted NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames are now handled correctly: #6009, #6007
  • DATAGRAM frames no longer starve ACKs, control frames and retransmissions: #5970
  • CancelRead now unblocks Read and Peek after receiving RESET_STREAM_AT: #6022
  • TryWriteAll no longer copies queued data quadratically: #6042, #6043
  • http3: canceling the first request to a host no longer cancels the shared dial: #6132
  • http3: bodies shorter than the announced Content-Length now fail with io.ErrUnexpectedEOF: #5913
  • http3: Content-Length is no longer added to 204 and 304 responses, and is now sent for requests with http.NoBody: #6032, #6029
  • http3: response writes that fail partway (e.g. on a write deadline) no longer corrupt the stream: #5993, #6002, #6001, #6003
  • http3: canceling an Extended CONNECT request now interrupts waiting for SETTINGS: #6020
  • qlog fixes:
    • incorrect or missing values for transport parameters, packet numbers, congestion metrics, timers, connection IDs and lengths: #6050, #6054, #6059, #6060, #6074, #6077, #6091, #6023, #5969
    • stateless resets are logged as remote closures: #6063
    • concurrently recorded events are written in order: #5956
    • traces of connections abandoned after version negotiation are closed: #6130

issue.body:
#### What type of PR is this?

- [ ] Enhancement / New Feature
- [x] Bug Fix
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] Optimization
- [ ] Test

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

The install library watched every CustomResourceDefinition. A change to an unrelated CRD queued a full istiod reconcile. The watch now accepts only CRDs in `*.istio.io` groups, which are the CRDs this library installs. Status updates still reconcile, because a CRD becomes ready in its status.

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes #2097

#### Additional information:

`TestIstioCRDWatchPredicate` accepts a `networking.istio.io` CRD on create, delete, and when its status becomes Established. A `cert-manager.io` CRD is rejected for those same events.

issue.body:
**Please provide a description of this PR:**

With `networkGateway` set, the `gateway` chart's Service exposes the ports from `networkGatewayPorts` (15021, 15443, 15012 and 15017 by default) and ignores `service.ports`. The NetworkPolicy template didn't follow that: it always built the traffic ingress rules from `service.ports`. So with `global.networkPolicy.enabled=true`, an east-west gateway only allowed 15021, 15020, 15090 and the default 80/443, and cross-network mTLS (15443), istiod (15012) and webhook (15017) traffic was dropped.

`helm template istio-eastwest manifests/charts/gateway --set networkGateway=network-1 --set global.networkPolicy.enabled=true` on master renders ports 15021, 80 and 443 for the main traffic; with this change it renders 15443, 15012 and 15017, using the `targetPort` from `networkGatewayPorts` and the same defaults as the Service. Without `networkGateway`, the output is unchanged.

Added the `gateway-network-gateway-networkpolicy` case to `TestRender` in `operator/pkg/helm` (network gateway with a remapped `tls` port and NetworkPolicy enabled). The golden fails against the master template and passes with the fix; `go test ./operator/pkg/helm/ ./operator/cmd/mesh/` passes.

Backport of #62748 to `release-1.31`.

**Please provide a description of this PR:**

A `DNS` or `DNS_ROUND_ROBIN` ServiceEntry attached to a waypoint can have no endpoints, for example when its `workloadSelector` matches no workloads. In this case, `buildCluster` returns `nil`, but `buildWaypointInboundVIPCluster` unconditionally dereferences the result, causing istiod to panic during CDS generation.

Handle the nil result and omit skipped clusters from the waypoint inbound cluster list, consistent with the existing outbound DNS cluster handling. This allows CDS generation to complete for the remaining clusters instead of crashing istiod.

The regression test covers both DNS resolution modes with HTTP, TLS, and protocol-sniffing ports, with and without matching workloads. It verifies that clusters without endpoints are omitted, other clusters are still generated, and DNS clusters with endpoints retain their expected discovery type and load assignment. A release note is included.

issue.body:
**Please provide a description of this PR:**

Gateways with the DNS proxy enabled (`ISTIO_META_ENABLE_DNS_SERVER=true`) receive an empty NDS name table.

#53286 / #53495 enabled the DNS server and name table for gateways (removing the sidecar-only check). Later, #54207 changed `BuildNameTable` to iterate `SidecarScope.EgressListeners` (mirroring LDS) so that all `model.Service`s for a host, e.g. multi-address ServiceEntries, are included. However, the default gateway `SidecarScope` has no egress listeners, so for gateways the loop yields no services and the table is always empty.

This change falls back to `SidecarScope.Services()` for router proxies whose scope has no egress listeners, so gateways get the same name table a sidecar with the default scope would. Sidecars (and any proxy with egress listeners) are unchanged.

Testing: added `TestNameTableGateway`, which fails without the fix (empty table) and passes with it; it checks that a gateway's table contains both a ClusterIP and a headless service and matches the sidecar's table. `go test ./pkg/dns/... ./pilot/pkg/xds/...` passes.

- [x] Networking

Release note added: `releasenotes/notes/gateway-dns-name-table.yaml`.

issue.title: ingress gateway: no supported way to set hostNetwork via IstioOperator or the gateway chart
issue.body:
### Goal

Run the ingress gateway bound directly to node ports 80/443 on **every node** (no kube-proxy in the data path), i.e. `hostNetwork` with one replica per node (DaemonSet-style).

### Current state

There is no supported way to express `hostNetwork` for the gateway:

* **IstioOperator** — `spec.components.ingressGateways[].k8s` (`KubernetesResourcesSpec`) has no `hostNetwork` field and no workload-kind field. The available fields are: `affinity`, `env`, `hpaSpec`, `imagePullPolicy`, `nodeSelector`, `podDisruptionBudget`, `podAnnotations`, `priorityClassName`, `readinessProbe`, `replicaCount`, `resources`, `service`, `strategy`, `tolerations`, `serviceAnnotations`, `overlays`.
* **Helm chart** `manifests/charts/gateway/values.yaml` exposes `kind` (so a DaemonSet can be requested) and `dnsPolicy`, but no `hostNetwork`.
* `k8s.overlays` cannot change the workload `kind` (Deployment → DaemonSet): an overlay with `kind: DaemonSet` is ignored and the component is still rendered as a `Deployment`.

A PR adding `hostNetwork` to the gateway chart (mirroring the existing `dnsPolicy` pattern) is open: #62201.

### Additional constraints that make this non-trivial

Binding a privileged port via the gateway also requires all of the following (each verified separately):

1. **The gateway listener port follows the gateway Service `targetPort`.** With the default Service (`80 -> 8080`) Envoy listens on 8080 even though the `Gateway` CR declares port 80. Setting `targetPort: 80/443` moves the listener to 80/443.
2. **`ISTIO_META_UNPRIVILEGED_POD` must not be `true`.** The chart sets it to `true`; when set, istiod silently drops privileged listener ports:

   ```
   buildGatewayListeners: skipping privileged gateway port 80 for node ... as it is an unprivileged pod
   gateway has zero listeners for node ...
   ```

   The gateway pod is `Ready` while having **zero listeners**, which is hard to diagnose. Adding `NET_BIND_SERVICE` does not change this — the check reads the `UnprivilegedPod` metadata (`pilot/pkg/model/context.go: IsUnprivileged()`), not the container capabilities.
3. **`NET_BIND_SERVICE` capability** is needed as well, since the proxy runs as uid 1337 and otherwise cannot bind < 1024.

### Request

Make this deployment model supported and documented — a `hostNetwork` field for the gateway chart (PR #62201), and either first-class support in the IstioOperator API or documentation of the recommended approach together with the ordering/requirements above (targetPort, `ISTIO_META_UNPRIVILEGED_POD`, `NET_BIND_SERVICE`).

issue.title: perf: reuse push request copies across queue merges

labels.name: user-8213b3f8/repo-e5e4d80a
labels.description: Denotes a PR that changes 100-499 lines, ignoring generated files.

issue.body:
Avoid repeatedly copying accumulated push requests for each connection. This removes quadratic copying as config, address, and waypoint sets grow, and reduces request/map allocations even for repeated updates to the same resources. Incoming requests remain unmodified, preserving the shared-request protection introduced in [#35193](https://github.com/istio/istio/pull/35193).

Savings keep increasing after three or more requests accumulate for one connection's next push in `PushQueue`, outside the debounce loop requests may arrive from separate debounced batches or bypass debouncing entirely (like `PILOT_ENABLE_EDS_DEBOUNCE=false`).

Note that with no merge or only two accumulated requests, no repeated copy is avoided and this change doesn't show any gains. Copy tracking **adds very little overhead** when there less than two merges (less than 3 updates) captured in benchmark results. But this can be a good trade off assuming less merges mean istio is already processing push requests faster than incoming updates.

### Benchmarks

`BenchmarkPushQueueEndpointFanout`: medians of five paired 500 ms runs.

| Benchmark subtest | Before time/op | After time/op | Time reduction | Before allocated MB/op | After allocated MB/op | Allocation-byte reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `updates=10/services=10` | 3.930 ms | 1.603 ms | 59.22% | 8.476 | 1.919 | 77.36% |
| `updates=100/services=100` | 185.859 ms | 16.006 ms | 91.39% | 453.581 | 13.535 | 97.02% |
| `updates=100/services=1` | 34.667 ms | 11.235 ms | 67.59% | 80.876 | 0.983 | 98.78% |
| `updates=2/services=100` | 3.363 ms | 3.395 ms | -0.95% | 7.060 | 7.135 | -1.06% |
| `updates=1/services=100` | 0.095 ms | 0.097 ms | -1.92% | 0.092 | 0.092 | -0.05% |

Sourced from github.com/quic-go/quic-go's releases.

v0.65.0

This release updates qlog to the latest IETF drafts, adds explicit stream credit release, and fixes a number of HTTP/3 and connection migration bugs.

  • qlog: events now follow draft-ietf-quic-qlog-quic-events-14 and draft-ietf-quic-qlog-h3-events-14: #6120

  • QUIC v2 key updates now use the correct quicv2 ku label: #5973
  • Connections using zero-length connection IDs no longer stop receiving packets after version negotiation: #6129
  • Switching paths now uses a new connection ID, fixing servers that kept sending to the old address after repeated NAT rebindings: #6015
  • Clients now send PATH_RESPONSE on the path the PATH_CHALLENGE was received on: #5980
  • Path.Probe now succeeds on an already validated path: #6019
  • Reordered and retransmitted NEW_CONNECTION_ID frames are now handled correctly: #6009, #6007
  • DATAGRAM frames no longer starve ACKs, control frames and retransmissions: #5970

  • http3: Content-Length is no longer added to 204 and 304 responses, and is now sent for requests with http.NoBody: #6032, #6029
  • http3: response writes that fail partway (e.g. on a write deadline) no longer corrupt the stream: #5993, #6002, #6001, #6003
  • http3: canceling an Extended CONNECT request now interrupts waiting for SETTINGS: #6020

    • stateless resets are logged as remote closures: #6063

issue.title: pilot: set :authority on InferencePool ext_proc gRPC calls

labels.name: user-8213b3f8/repo-c2a5577a
labels.description: Denotes a PR that changes 10-29 lines, ignoring generated files.

issue.body:
**Please provide a description of this PR:**

The per-route `ext_proc` override generated for an `InferencePool` only sets `EnvoyGrpc.cluster_name`. Envoy uses the cluster name as the `:authority` of the gRPC stream when `authority` is unset, so the endpoint picker receives:

```
:authority: outbound|9002||<epp-service>.<ns>.svc.cluster.local
```

`|` is not a valid URI character. Servers that validate `:authority` (RFC 9113 §8.3.1; e.g. Rust `h2`/`tonic`) reset the stream with `PROTOCOL_ERROR`, and every request through the pool fails with 500 (`ext_proc_error_gRPC_error_14 ... remote_reset`). The reference Go endpoint picker does not validate the header, which is why this went unnoticed.

Set `authority` to the endpoint picker service FQDN, as the tracing and access-log gRPC services already do. SNI is unaffected (it comes from the cluster transport socket).

Reproduced on 1.28.3 with the NVIDIA Dynamo endpoint picker: before, the EPP logs `h2::server: malformed headers: malformed authority (b"outbound|9002||mgaie-epp.p-dynamo-test.svc.cluster.local"): invalid uri character` and the gateway returns 500; with `authority` set to the FQDN the same requests return 200.

The same code is on release-1.28, 1.29 and 1.30.

issue.body:
**Please provide a description of this PR:**

Fixes #59490

The gateway chart can deploy the gateway as a DaemonSet (`kind: DaemonSet`), but there is no way to configure the DaemonSet `updateStrategy`. The only knob is `strategy`, which is rendered as the Deployment field `spec.strategy`. A DaemonSet does not have that field, so setting it with `kind: DaemonSet` produces an invalid manifest.

As a result, DaemonSet gateways always use the Kubernetes default (`RollingUpdate`, `maxSurge: 0`, `maxUnavailable: 1`): the old pod on a node is removed before the new one starts. This matters most for the main reason to run the gateway as a DaemonSet, `externalTrafficPolicy: Local`. While a node has no local gateway pod, the external load balancer still sends traffic to it until its health check notices, and those connections are dropped. With `maxSurge: 1` and `maxUnavailable: 0` the new pod becomes ready on the same node before the old one is terminated, so the node always has a local endpoint.

This PR adds an `updateStrategy` value, following the same pattern as the ztunnel and istio-cni charts (#55769):

- `templates/deployment.yaml`: render `spec.updateStrategy` from `.Values.updateStrategy` when it is set, the same way `strategy` is rendered.
- `values.yaml`: add `updateStrategy: {}`. The default is empty, so the rendered output for existing installs does not change.
- `values.schema.json`: allow `updateStrategy` as an object.
- `operator/pkg/helm`: add the `gateway-daemonset-update-strategy` golden test.
- Release note.

Example:

```yaml
kind: DaemonSet
updateStrategy:
  type: RollingUpdate
  rollingUpdate:
    maxSurge: 1
    maxUnavailable: 0
```

`strategy` is left as is to keep this change additive. A separate value is used instead of reusing `strategy`, because the two fields have different types (`Recreate` exists only for Deployments, `OnDelete` only for DaemonSets).

Testing:

- `go test ./operator/pkg/helm/ -run TestRender` passes.
- `helm lint` passes with `kind: DaemonSet` and `updateStrategy` set.
